Meta subscriptions now show their usage and plan as Claude and Codex do. An account can be tested with one request, and any request can be inspected before it is sent. Named clients can be served another model and can read a status line. The binary is smaller despite the new features, config files no longer go through libyaml, and named-client spend no longer rescans the month every 30 seconds.

## Changes

- **Meta subscriptions.** Signed-in Meta accounts count as subscriptions on the dashboard, in the iPhone app and in the pools.
  - Meta has no usage endpoint, so Fusebox reads the 5-hour and weekly windows from the `response.subscription_usage` frame that every Meta response streams. It checks idle accounts through Meta's free key mint. The last reading survives restarts.
  - The plan shows as the tier name saved at sign-in ("Max Usage") instead of "Device code".
  - A lapsed subscription reads "subscription inactive" until the mint reports it active again.
  - Meta's unreported cache writes count as zero, so Meta requests are no longer stored as partial and get a price.
  - Muse Spark is priced at Meta's rates. Meta publishes no price for Muse Wonder Full, so it is estimated at Muse Wonder's rate and counts "with assumptions" (catalogue t3-2026-11-04.1).
- **Billing days set by hand.** Claude and Meta give no billing date, so their sign-in card has "Set billing date".
  - The day repeats monthly, or yearly for Claude Pro, and feeds the renewal line, the overview, the iPhone app and the reminder.
  - "Cancelled" ends the subscription on the next billing day.
  - After a plan change the date shows as an estimate to check, with no reminder, until it is saved again.
- **Day-before reminder.** `notifications.renewals-day-before` (off by default) sends the renewal reminder a day ahead, beside or instead of the two-day one.
- **The last account left after a stall.** A first-token stall used to bench the account for two minutes. With only one account, the client's retries then got "all accounts are rate limited".
  - An account now sits out a model only when another account can take it. Otherwise the retry reaches it again.
  - With no other account free, an attempt waits twice the first-token deadline (240 s by default).
  - A request left without an account because of a stall gets a 503 that names the stall, with a `Retry-After` of at most a minute.
- **Model map for named clients.** `model-map` rewrites the model a client asks for before routing, as in `{claude-opus-*: claude-sonnet-5-5}`. Batch agents can keep asking for Opus and be served Sonnet.
  - Patterns match the base model case-insensitively. An exact pattern beats a wildcard, and the longer literal wins.
  - Two equally specific wildcards that can match the same model are a config error.
  - The client's model list applies to the mapped model on every route, `count_tokens` included.
- **Inspect a request.** `POST /api/inspect` (management key) shows what Fusebox would send upstream for a request body. That covers the model after `model-map` and model groups, the route and account, and the URL, headers and body with credentials redacted, or else the refusal the client would get.
  - It sends nothing, refreshes no token, records no usage and takes no routing turn.
  - The Models page's Try a model card has an Inspect mode.
- **Test an account.** A Test button (`POST /api/accounts/{id}/test`) sends one small request to that account only, with its cheapest model, at most once a minute. It uses quota and may start a 5-hour window, which the drawer says.
- **Status for client keys.** `GET /v1/fusebox/status` gives any client key the combined quota pools, account counts and next resets, without account names. `?format=line` returns one line for a Claude Code status line.
- **Refused usage checks.** Three refused usage reads (401 or 403) within half an hour become an account error fault. They count only once a forced token refresh is refused too.
- **Server-tool fees.** Claude's web search, web fetch and code-execution calls, and Responses web search calls, are counted. Their per-call fees are priced on top of the token cost.
- **Banked resets** show "prioritized" only when another subscription of the same provider exists.
- **Client updates** (#48): Claude Code 2.1.318, Codex 0.166.0, Grok Build 1.0.70, Muse Code 1.4.14, Devin 3000.11.234 and Antigravity 2.29.0. `GET /api/client-identities` lists the names (never the values) of headers Fusebox drops.
- **Config YAML** is read by Fusebox's own reader on yaml-rust2, so serde_yaml and unsafe-libyaml are gone (#42). It reads every config that serde_yaml did, in the same way; this was checked against a corpus and 40,000 generated documents.
- **Smaller and lighter.**
  - The x86-64 Linux binary is 0.8 MB smaller than v0.13.0's (17.8 MB), with the new features included:
    - Time zones come from jiff's bundled database instead of chrono-tz, whose tables were 1 MB of pointers relocated at every start.
    - Unused dependency features are off, and bundled C code has no unwind tables.
  - Named-client tokens and spend come from hourly totals that the database keeps current. Before, every 30 seconds the month was rescanned while requests waited for it; on a month of production data that took 590 ms, and now takes 0.35 ms.
- **Tests.** Upstream requests are pinned byte for byte for every client format and account kind (43 goldens). Property tests cover YAML, SSE, the schema cleaner and translation.
- **Also:**
  - tokio 1.53.3 for a RUSTSEC advisory (#47).
  - [docs/moving.md](https://github.com/DigitalPals/Fusebox/blob/v0.14.0/docs/moving.md) explains how to move Fusebox to another machine.

## Upgrading

- **Database.** The usage database stays on schema 5.
  - The first start adds the `usage_client_totals` table and three triggers. It fills the table from a day before the current month, which took 63 ms on a 2 GB database.
  - v0.13.0 runs on the result and keeps the totals current.
  - v0.13.0's `usage compact`, `usage downgrade` and keeper import commands can't write to the database while the triggers exist. To use them after going back, first drop the triggers `usage_client_totals_insert`, `_delete` and `_update`, then the table. Any SQLite client can do that.
- **New settings:**
  - `notifications.renewals-day-before` (off by default);
  - `model-map` on a named client. Older releases refuse a config that uses it, so remove it before going back.
- **New routes:** `POST /api/inspect`, `POST /api/accounts/{id}/test` and `GET /v1/fusebox/status`.
- **API changes:** `/api/client-identities` adds `dropped_headers`, and Meta quotas carry `plan_name` and `subscription_inactive`.
- **Time zones.** The time-zone data is now 2026e, so Usage-page days move in zones whose rules changed, such as America/Vancouver from 1 November 2026 and Africa/Casablanca from 20 September 2026.
- **Source builds.** An x86-64 Linux release build now gets packed relocations and identical-code folding whenever its toolchain can link and run them. Such a binary needs glibc 2.36 where it runs; `FUSEBOX_PLAIN_LINK=1` builds without them.
- **iPhone app.** Its source has two fixes: stale answers can't come back after a sign-out or reconnect, and the tests stay off a signed-in simulator. They ship with the next TestFlight build.

Validation: 985 Rust and 180 dashboard tests passed, with CI on Linux, macOS and Windows. Production has run this code since 5 November 2026.

[Full comparison with v0.13.0](https://github.com/DigitalPals/Fusebox/compare/v0.13.0...v0.14.0).
